cohort: 258,800 twin pregnancies without reported congenital anomalies from the US matched multiple birth data 1995-2000
finding: The risk of perinatal death for second-born twins compared to first-born twins was dependent on their relative birth size, with higher risks observed in second twins who weighed progressively less than their first-born counterparts.
mod_finding: While perinatal mortality rates did not differ significantly by birth order for cesarean deliveries or preterm vaginal deliveries, second twins had a significantly higher perinatal mortality rate in term vaginal deliveries.
